what_it_is.prose: Aequs Limited is a precision-engineering group founded in 2000 by Aravind Melligeri and headquartered in Belagavi, Karnataka, where it built and operates India's first precision-engineering and aerospace Special Economic Zone (250+ acres). Aequs' differentiator is an integrated 'forge-to-fly' cluster that co-locates forging, machining, surface treatment and assembly within about 500 metres, compressing a supply chain that would otherwise span thousands of kilometres. In aerospace — historically 85-89% of revenue — Aequs makes flight-critical components and assemblies for Airbus (a ~15-year 'D2P' relationship), Boeing (Tier-1 since 2017), Safran (engine components), Collins Aerospace and Spirit AeroSystems, and supplies roughly 40% of the Airbus A320 landing-gear components that are manufactured in France. It reports an aerospace order book of around USD 814 million through 2031 and aerospace-segment EBITDA margins near 24%. In June 2026 Aequs signed a further engine-parts agreement with Safran and in May 2026 inaugurated a new facility for narrow-body aircraft components. Aequs listed on the NSE/BSE in December 2025 through a ₹922 crore IPO (fresh issue ₹670 crore plus offer for sale) priced at ₹124 per share, with proceeds largely used to repay debt. Beyond aerospace, Aequs has diversified into consumer-electronics casings, toys (Hasbro, Mattel/Spin Master) and cookware (a Tramontina JV).

deployments_procurement.summary: Aequs is an export-oriented Tier-1 aerospace components supplier to global OEMs rather than a platform builder; its India relevance is as a sovereign forge-to-assembly base and one of the country's largest private aerospace exporters. Contract-level detail is limited to analyst notes and IPO disclosures.

faq.question: What makes Aequs' Belagavi aerospace SEZ distinctive?
faq.answer: Aequs built and runs India's first precision-engineering and aerospace Special Economic Zone in Belagavi, Karnataka — a 250+ acre integrated cluster that co-locates forging, machining, surface treatment and assembly within about 500 metres. This 'forge-to-fly' model lets Aequs turn raw metal into flight-critical finished parts on one campus, compressing a supply chain that would otherwise span thousands of kilometres and making it one of India's largest private aerospace exporters.

faq.question: Which global aerospace customers does Aequs supply and how big is its order book?
faq.answer: Aequs is a Tier-1 supplier to Airbus (a roughly 15-year 'D2P' relationship), Boeing (Tier-1 since 2017), Safran (engine components, expanded via a June 2026 agreement), Collins Aerospace and Spirit AeroSystems. It supplies around 40% of the Airbus A320 landing-gear components made in France, and analyst notes cite an aerospace order book of about USD 814 million running through 2031 at roughly 24% aerospace EBITDA margins.

faq.question: Is Aequs listed?
faq.answer: Yes. Aequs listed on the NSE/BSE in December 2025 through a ₹922 crore IPO (a fresh issue of ₹670 crore plus an offer for sale) priced at ₹124 per share, with proceeds used largely to repay debt. The company was founded in 2000 by Aravind Melligeri, who remains Executive Chairman.
